title: Acute lung injury induces sustained neuroinflammation and dysfunction in the brainstem nucleus of the solitary tract of rats
title_zh: 急性肺损伤导致大鼠孤束核持续性神经炎症与功能障碍
abstract: Abstract Background Acute lung injury (ALI) causes profound pulmonary inflammation and is increasingly associated with neurological symptoms, suggesting that inflammatory signalling extends beyond the lungs to affect central nervous system circuits. However, the molecular and functional consequences of ALI in brainstem regions involved in respiratory control remain poorly defined. Here, we examined the impact of bleomycin-induced ALI on the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), the primary brainstem termination site of vagal sensory afferents from the lungs. Main body Using a rat model, a single intratracheal dose of bleomycin (7.5 mg/ kg) induced acute lung inflammation, persistent tissue pathology, and altered respiratory parameters lasting up to 28 days. Transcriptomic profiling of the NTS revealed widespread gene expression changes at both day 7 and day 28. Ranked gene set enrichment analysis showed that early transcriptional changes were characterised by positive enrichment of synaptic signalling and neurotransmission-related processes, together with negative enrichment of metabolic, lipid catabolic, and immune-associated pathways. By day 28, positively enriched pathways shifted towards mitochondrial and energy-generating processes, whereas negatively enriched pathways implicated synaptic organisation, neuronal guidance, and cell adhesion-related biology. Morphometric analysis of IBA1-positive microglia demonstrated significant changes in microglial morphology within the NTS at both time points, consistent with a reactive phenotype. Functionally, in vivo microinjections of capsaicin or L-glutamic acid into the NTS evoked significantly attenuated respiratory responses in bleomycin-treated rats compared with controls. Conclusion Bleomycin-induced ALI drives sustained neuroinflammatory and functional disruption in the NTS, a key brainstem hub for pulmonary vagal signalling. These findings provide new evidence for lung-to-brain communication in ALI and identify molecular pathways that may underlie impaired reflex control and broader neurological morbidity associated with respiratory disease.
abstract_zh: 背景：急性肺损伤（ALI）引起严重的肺部炎症，并越来越多地与神经系统症状相关，提示炎症信号可超出肺部，影响中枢神经系统回路。然而，ALI对参与呼吸调控的脑干区域的分子和功能后果尚不清楚。本研究考察了由溶菌酶诱导的ALI对孤束核（NTS）的影响，NTS是肺部迷走神经感觉传入的主要脑干终止位点。方法：使用大鼠模型，单次气管内注射溶菌酶（7.5 mg/kg）诱导急性肺炎，导致持续的组织病理改变和呼吸参数异常，持续至28天。对NTS进行转录组分析显示，在第7天和第28天均出现广泛的基因表达变化。基因集富集分析显示，早期转录变化以突触信号和神经递质相关过程的正向富集为特征，同时代谢、脂质分解和免疫相关通路的负向富集。到第28天，正向富集通路转向线粒体和能量生成过程，而负向富集通路涉及突触组织、神经引导和细胞粘附相关生物学。IBA1阳性小胶质细胞的形态学分析显示，在两时间点NTS内小胶质细胞形态显著改变，符合反应性表型。功能上，向NTS进行体内微注射辣椒素或L-谷氨酸，导致溶菌酶处理大鼠的呼吸反应显著减弱，与对照组相比。结论：溶菌酶诱导的ALI在NTS中驱动持续的神经炎症和功能紊乱，NTS是肺部迷走神经信号的关键脑干枢纽。这些发现为ALI中的肺脑通信提供了新证据，并识别了可能导致呼吸疾病相关反射控制受损和更广泛神经系统并发症的分子通路。
